metadata.name: Ecodesign for Shell (sh, bash, zsh)
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for shell scripts: no process spawned per line, no polling, streamed data, temporary files cleaned up.

processus.name: Shell — processes
processus.description: A shell script pays for every process it starts; in a loop, that is the whole cost (RGESN Algorithms).

rules.title: Command substitution inside a loop
rules.description: Every $(...) forks a process, and a fork costs more than the work most of these commands do. In a loop over a thousand lines that is a thousand processes to compute what one awk pass would have produced in one.
rules.recommendation: Do the work in one pass: awk, sed or a single pipeline. Where the loop must stay, hoist whatever does not depend on the iteration out of it.

example.bad: for f in $(ls); do wc -l "$f"; done

rules.note: A substitution in the loop header is evaluated once and is fine; one in the body runs on every iteration. The pattern sees the line, not the position, so check which of the two you have.

rules.title: Useless use of cat
rules.description: cat file | command starts a process and a pipe to hand over what the command can open by itself. It is small, and it is in every script, run every time.
rules.recommendation: Redirect instead: command < file, or pass the filename as an argument.

rules.title: Chained greps and cuts
rules.description: grep | grep | cut | awk starts four processes and copies the data through three pipes, where a single awk reads it once.
rules.recommendation: Collapse the chain into one awk or sed pass, as long as it stays readable. Readability wins over a saved fork.

attente.name: Shell — waiting and I/O
attente.description: Never wait actively, never grow a file without bound (RGESN Backend/Hosting).

rules.title: Polling loop
rules.description: A loop that sleeps and re-tests keeps a shell, and often a subprocess, alive doing nothing. Left in a cron job or a container entrypoint, it runs for the lifetime of the machine.
rules.recommendation: Block on the event instead: wait for the PID, inotifywait, a queue, or a signal. Where polling is the only option, widen the interval and give the loop a bound.
rules.note: Only sleep is looked for: a while loop reading a stream is not polling, and flagging it would fire on every read loop in a repository. A sleep between retries with a bounded count is legitimate, so read the loop before acting.

rules.title: Temporary file with no cleanup
rules.description: A temporary file created without a trap survives every early exit and every failure. On a build agent or a container they accumulate until the disk fills.
rules.recommendation: Pair every mktemp with a trap that removes it on EXIT, so the cleanup happens on the error paths too.
rules.note: A single trap anywhere in the file silences the rule, even when another mktemp goes uncleaned. Check that every temporary path is covered, not just the first.

rules.title: Unbounded output to a log or a file
rules.description: A command appending to a file with no rotation and no bound fills the disk slowly and invisibly, and the backups carry it too.
rules.recommendation: Bound what you write: a log level, rotation, or a retention job. A script that writes a log should also say who deletes it.
